correctness.rationale: The source FOAF equation with diagonal unit weights yields (W²)_ij=2w_ij+S_ij, and two exact comparison inequalities. Exponential extinction below c*=N/[2(N+1)] makes the opinion generator integrable and its limiting stochastic fundamental matrix invertible, precluding new consensus. At c*, every within-component tie decays between positive multiples of 1/t; uniform positivity after the logarithmic time change implies consensus. Above c*, logistic persistence plus uniform stochastic path mixing gives exponential consensus. Graph-component invariance, all-N quantifiers, endpoints and the explicit N=2 case were reconstructed. An accompanying checker passed 10,080 rational comparisons and 9 full ODE examples; finite tests are corroboration, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: An exact all-N structural boundary determines whether time-evolving social ties transmit enough cumulative influence for consensus. The critical case is qualitatively surprising: all ties vanish and yet every original connected component achieves agreement. The opposite subcritical obstruction holds for every initially nonconstant connected profile, not only one example; supercritical exponential consensus closes the classification. The FOAF model and persistence-vs-extinction question are naturally motivated by the original social-network literature.
